name: Sardine Melt

instructions.primary_message: Finely dice the celery. Finely dice the yellow onion. Very finely mince the garlic. Finely dice the celery rib. Zest the lemon.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 ribs celery
1 medium yellow onion
2 medium cloves garlic
1 celery rib
1 lemon

instructions.primary_message: For the Celery Confit (Optional): In a small saucepan, combine celery, onion, olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Set over medium heat and cook, stirring often, until the vegetables’ water has been released and fully cooked off and the vegetables have become meltingly tender, about 30 minutes; reduce heat at any point to prevent browning. Set aside.
For the Sandwich: In a small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, minced onion, garlic, herbs, celery, and lemon zest until very well combined. Season with salt and pepper.

Spread about 2 tablespoons of the prepared mayonnaise on one slice of bread. Arrange as many sardines from the tin as you can fit on top. Top with a few additional dollops of the mayo along with about 2 tablespoons of the celery confit, if using. Lightly squeeze the lemon wedge to release a few drops of juice on top, then finish with a layer of cheese and close the sandwich. Reserve extra mayo and celery confit for additional sandwiches or another use.

Add 1 tablespoon olive oil to a skillet and heat over medium heat until it swirls around and lightly coats the skillet surface. Add sandwich and cook, pressing down very gently and moving around as needed for even browning, until first side is well toasted and crisp, about 3 minutes.

Carefully flip sandwich, add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to skillet, and cook second side, pressing gently and swirling as needed for even browning, until bread is well toasted and crisp and cheese is melted, about 3 minutes longer; if bread is toasting faster than cheese is melting, reduce heat and cook for longer to allow the cheese to melt. Transfer to a serving plate, cut sandwich in half, and serve.

description: Using only pantry and fridge staples, this gooey, melty sandwich features tender sardines in place of the more classic tuna, a garlicky mayo, and plenty of drippy cheese.
notes:
Optional substitutions: finely minced quick-pickled red onion → raw red onion; minced dill → flat-leaf parsley; Sliced cheese → shredded cheddar cheese or Gruyère cheese

Notes: Feel free to substitute fennel root for the celery if you have it. It will be delicious (you can use the fronds in the mayo in place of, or in addition to, the other herbs).
author: Daniel Gritzer
